newsitem.title: USA: Blood spoils from U.S. parcel delivery strike.
newsitem.headline: Blood spoils from U.S. parcel delivery strike.

text.p: U.S. blood banks have destroyed 100 gallons of spoiled blood and hospitals have postponed some operations because of the United Parcel Service (UPS) strike, the largest blood network said.

The strike, by some 185,000 UPS delivery workers, could eventually cause severe blood shortages in the United States, added Jim MacPherson, executive director of America's Blood Centers, in a faxed statement received Friday.

The strike, over the proportion of part-time workers at UPS and pension fund arrangements, is in its 12th day. Talks between UPS and the Teamsters union continued on Friday morning amid signs that they had new proposals to discuss.
"More than 800 units (pints) of blood and blood components have spoiled and been destroyed because of delays in inter-city shipments since the UPS strike began," the statement by the network said.

The blood centers mainly use FedEx and Airborne Express to move their blood around but these carriers can no longer guarantee overnight delivery because of the extra business the UPS strike has brought them, it said.

America's Blood Centers collect about 5.4 million pints (1.4 million litres) a year, 46 percent of the nation's blood supply. Only about five percent of the blood needs shipping from one center to another.

The network suggested its blood banks set up mobile collection units near UPS picket lines so that striking UPS workers can donate their blood. One bank in Louisville, Kentucky, has already done this, the statement said.
